flags.name: repo
flags.description: path to the repository to inspect

flags.name: terms
flags.description: absolute path to the folder holding this project's .inspector.json, Dockerfile.inspector and check script, for a repository none of the three may be committed to; omitted when the repository carries them itself

flags.name: no-stamp
flags.description: takes no value; publish a green result as usual but post no commit status at all, for a repository whose CI must not be touched

flags.name: branch
flags.description: pull request branch to publish after a green result

flags.name: expected-tip
flags.description: commit origin's copy of the branch is expected to be at, so a rewritten branch is published with force-with-lease; omitted when the branch was never published or was not rewritten

flags.name: pr-title
flags.description: pull request title to open after a green result

flags.name: pr-body-file
flags.description: path to a file containing the pull request body

flags.name: vendor
flags.description: the reviewer's vendor, for judging the change's test edits; its key is read from <VENDOR>_API_KEY

flags.name: model
flags.description: the reviewer's model, named by the same vendor

buildSecrets.source: inspector's own environment: one variable per name the key lists, set by whoever invokes inspector
buildSecrets.note: fabrica reads each value from ~/.fabrica/brain.env and sets it on the inspector child's environment; only names ever appear in a config, an argv, a log, a report or a message

buildArgs.entry: NAME to {file} or {file, pattern}, where file is repository-relative
buildArgs.source: the repository under check, read at the commit being checked - never the working tree and never another tree
buildArgs.patternSemantics: matched one trimmed line at a time, first matching line winning, taking the first capture group or the whole match when the pattern has none; with no pattern the value is the file's first non-empty line, trimmed. Never a (?m) inline flag: fabrica matches these with JavaScript's engine and inspector with Go's RE2, and (?m) is a syntax error in the first
buildArgs.unresolved: a declared name whose file is absent, whose file matches nothing, or whose value could not be a Docker tag is not passed at all, so the Dockerfile's own ARG default stands
buildArgs.note: fabrica register writes `ARG RUBY_VERSION=<version>` above the first FROM and `FROM ruby:${RUBY_VERSION}`, plus the matching entry here, so the version an image is built on follows the repository's own .ruby-version / .node-version / .python-version / go.mod rather than a number typed into a Dockerfile (fabrica issue #355). The ARG always carries a default, so a build that passes no value - an older inspector, a hand docker build - produces exactly the image the literal tag produced. Fabrica resolves the same entries for its own machine-image build, from that build's context, and hashes them into that image's stamp so a version bump rebuilds it too
